## BOOK 1 of 2: TOMMY (Joseph Hocking, 1916, Hodder & Stoughton)

### Front matter / Note by author
- Author admired "Tommy"; met him before enlisting while addressing recruiting meetings for 6+ months; visited him in training camps, France and Flanders (La Bassee, Neuve Chapelle, Ypres; stood in front trenches <100 yards from German sandbags).
- Only a small part is imagination; nearly every incident told by Tommy himself; tale is fact.
- Dated: Priors' Corner, Totteridge, Herts, February 1916.
- Other Hocking titles listed: All for a Scrap of Paper; Dearer Than Life; Facing Fearful Odds; O'er Moor and Fen; The Wilderness; Rosaleen O'Hara; The Soul of Dominie Wildthorne; Follow the Gleam; David Baring; The Trampled Cross.

### Ch. I (Sunday, first Sunday in June 1914; Brunford Town Hall clock)
- Tom Pollard leaves home in Dixon Street ~3:30 p.m. toward the **Thorn and Thistle** pub. Crosses tram lines in St. George's Street; Liverpool Road.
- **Polly Powell**: buxom, bold-eyed, red-cheeked, ~24, daughter of landlord **Enoch Powell**. Wears highly coloured dress. Says Jim Scott came; Jim Dixon coming to tea. Tells Tom his father says he has brains (3 prizes at Mechanics' Institute last winter); if he manufactured on own, "he'd make brass." Father has saved money. Polly calls Tom "Ay, Tom lad."
- Tom says he has "an appointment"; Polly suspects Alice Lister. Tom promised a Tackler's job (foreman-like).
- **Alice Lister**: ~20, refined, intelligent, large eyes; daughter of a small manufacturer (once weaver; "doin' vary weel"). Sang contralto; pianist; French and German classes; sang at concerts. Sunday School teacher-type girl.
- Girls' remarks: Emily Bilson mocks Tom; "young landlord at the Bull and Butcher" mentioned re Polly.
- Tom and Alice walk up Liverpool Road, enter **Scott's Park**. Alice gives ultimatum: give up Alice or give up Thorn and Thistle. Tom: "Harry Briarfield was up at your house to supper." Alice: "Duty, God." Tom chooses Waterman/Polly; Alice: "I see your choice is made"; "Good-bye, Tom."
- **Harry Waterman**: well-dressed, tall, florid, light-brown hair; claims squire's son from Warwickshire; studied in German university; told Tom religion only for ignorant people and women; invites Tom to "club at the Rose and Crown" at seven. Tom chooses him.
- Polly takes Tom back to tea. Tom drunk that night; mother **Martha Pollard** scolds ("Thou'st gi'en up a nice lass for a brazen-faaced 'uzzy"). Father **Ezekiel Pollard** (weaver, 30 shillings/week). Tom ~23.
- Tom had been teetotal; Sunday School abandoned.

### Ch. II (June 1914 – Jan 1915)
- Brunford: large cotton town in Lancashire; "boom in trade."
- Youth remarks; Jim Parkin says Tom spent four shillings at Thorn and Thistle.
- Manufacturers on Mechanics' Institute steps discuss Germany and war.
- Crown Prince of Austria murdered; Sir Edward Grey mentioned. Early Aug 1914 England declares war.
- Enoch Powell: "I give them about six weeks."
- Lord Kitchener's call for half a million men.
- Waterman (back from absence) says he will enlist (commission), says Germans will beat England. Tom: "Think of our Navy." Waterman walks off.
- **Herr Shweitzer**: young German, Brunford resident, given farewell dinner at **Bull and Butcher** hotel; says Kaiser/Wilhelm II will rule England. An Englishman punches him ("That for you and your Kaiser!"); German's jaw broken; hospitalised.
- Tom holds back; **Elijah Butterworth** (three sons in army) challenges him; Tom: "I'm noan a coward."
- Dec 1914-Jan 1915: Tom attends two recruiting meetings; declines while Polly persuades him to stay. New Year recruiting meeting at great hall of Mechanics' Institute; speaker (man who had been to Belgium) appeals: "Who will be the first?" Tom: "No! By God, no!" walks forward and gives name. Thus Tom becomes soldier.
- Mother: "Ay, tha mun be sent to Lancaster asylum." (footnote about incident at Lancashire city.)

### Ch. III (Jan–June 1915)
- Tom tells Polly (midnight); she says "Thou'st noan been such a fool?" Tom asks her to stay true; she says "Of course I'll be true to you."
- Next morning Tom meets Alice Lister on way to Town Hall; she praises him ("splendid"); he jokes about young parson courting her.
- Tom joins **Loyal North Lancashires**; training camp at Lancashire town ~30 miles from Brunford. Grows 2 inches, chest +3 inches in 3 months.
- Drunk and disorderly; punished by colonel (stern but kind; says "Make a beast of yourself?"; suggests Y.M.C.A.).
- **Robert Penrose**: Cornish, public-school (Charterhouse, five years), gentleman ranker, best boxer, refused commission; tells Tom he is making an ass of himself; invites him to Y.M.C.A.
- **Alec McPhail**: Scottish, Black Watch; kilts; "wee lassie" date; philosopher who once read Ingersoll; mother godly; father elder in old U.P. Kirk; drinks whisky.
- Tom attends Y.M.C.A. entertainments; learns French ("Je suis, Vous êtes, Nous sommes, Ils sont").
- Battalion moves to Surrey, ~May 1915 (Godalming; Penrose's old school Charterhouse on hill). Camp of huts; Y.M.C.A. huts (six huts, 1000 men each).
- Penrose gazetted and moves to another camp ~4 miles away.
- Tom on leave in Brunford; with Polly at Thorn and Thistle; drinks beer.
- Waterman seen as Lieutenant in Surrey camp; Tom salutes "Mr. Waterman."
- Mother's letter: Polly walking out with Jim Dixon; Polly "is the image of her mother"; "sack her."

### Ch. IV (Surrey camp; then France)
- Tom's report on French; Y.M.C.A. "fair God-send."
- McPhail drinks at wayside pub near camp; Tom criticises him. McPhail confesses fear, whisky courage; says "it's either whisky or releegion."
- Farewell meetings at Y.M.C.A. huts; a special speaker: "Possibly many of you are going to your death... You need a Captain, a Guide, a Saviour." Canteen scene: men drinking; pale refined lad: "I know she would be praying for me."
- McPhail: "I am giving my heart to God."
- Folkestone, troopship; Destroyer escort; landed at Boulogne; troop train; march; artillery and aeroplanes near front.

### Ch. V (Ypres salient)
- Sergeant (served ~20 years) describes Second Ypres/“battle of Wipers”; Jack Johnson and Black Maria; Cloth Hall, Cathedral destroyed; poison gas; Germans shoot surrendering troops; young lieutenant "No, my lads, you are going to kingdom come."
- Lancashire lad killed by sniper ("Hampstead Heath Bank Holiday skylarking").
- Tom's first front-line bayonet fight; young officer volunteers, rescues wounded German who then shoots him dead (footnote: incident actually happened).
- Waterman seen again as staff officer by canal; Tom salutes.
- Tom on sentry duty at night, prays: "O God!—O God!—O God!"; thinks of Alice praying.
- Named missing comrades: Jim Bates, Arthur Wadge, Bill Perkins, George Wilson.

### Ch. VI (Alice's night)
- Harry Briarfield (24, partner in father George Briarfield's mill) proposes to Alice; she asks days to think. Minister **Mr. Skelton** (bachelor) earlier proposed; refused.
- Parents George Lister and Mrs. Lister; Mrs. Lister had earlier refused William Pott.
- Alice prays at midnight: "O God, save him!" — simultaneous with Tom's prayer.

### Ch. VII (Night attack; McPhail)
- German voice from trench warns: "you Lancashires are going to attack us at six o'clock to-morrow morning, eleven hundred strong." Tom reports to subaltern; Colonel interrogates; attack goes ahead with Black Watch support; no treachery found by officers. Sergeant Ashworth praises Tom (declined lance-corporal stripe).
- Tom's conversion: "from that time he felt the reality of God."
- Alec McPhail wounded; dies in hospital near Ypres (road to Cassel). Last words: "It's a' richt"; Psalm 23 recited; "Jesu, Lover of my soul" sung; McPhail's mother in Highlands; Tom writes to her.

### Ch. VIII (Waterman's treachery)
- Colonel Blount and Major Blundell; General Withers at Divisional HQ; Brigadier. Achan in the camp.
- Tom sees Waterman (captain/staff officer) with officers; Blount cross-examines Tom.
- Night: Waterman (Major Blundell says "Good night, Waterman") throws a white paper with weight across parapet; Tom grabs him; Lieutenant **Penrose** arrives with men (Jackson takes revolver).
- Tom crawls into No-man's-Land, fights German who grabbed paper; breaks his shoulder blade with football trick; wounded in left arm and right shoulder; reaches trench. Major Blundell: "you've done the trick." Nick (Brunford friend) present.
- Colonel Blount visits; mentions Waterman "deserves a worse death."

### Ch. IX (Court martial; execution)
- Tom's evidence; Waterman admits being German (born English, two n's in name "Waterman" → German spelling); says "Shame in feeling that I have served the Fatherland!"; executed by firing squad at a wall.

### Ch. X (Return to Brunford, Dec 1915)
- Newspaper headlines "Heroism of a Lancashire Lad"; Tom recommended for D.C.M.; Colonel Blount: "I'm proud of you."
- Tom arrives Brunford Saturday in December on leave via London (King's Cross 10 o'clock train). Crowd cheers. Refuses Polly's invitation ("I don't want to play gooseberry"); Rose and Crown refused; "following the example of the King" re teetotal.
- Parents pray; Tom says "Then let us kneel down and thank God."

### Ch. XI (Reunion; departure)
- Church service; meets Alice in vestibule; walk home up Liverpool Road; "I never was [engaged to Harry Briarfield]"; reconciliation; Tom: "I am only a poor Tommy with a bob a day"; will wait "till the war is over."
- George Lister agrees; Mrs. Lister approves.
- Tom and Alice at Waterloo; Kipling's story "The Ship That Found Herself"; "au revoir"; train leaves; prayer "God help me to do my bit, and then take me back to her."
- Narrator saw him off at Waterloo.

## BOOK 2 of 2: WHEN FREEMEN SHALL STAND (Nelson S. Bond, Fantastic Adventures, Nov 1943)

### Ch. I (Laboratory, 1942-ish, Fort Knox era)
- **Lt. Stephen "Steve" Duane**: chemical engineer/chemist; **Chuck Lafferty**: sergeant, lab assistant. Officer ranks/nickname "Lootenant."
- Gas-mask guard; **Eric von Rath**: German spy, disguised as guard; leveled .44 automatic. Vial of anesthetic **methioprane** (from swamp-musk seed-pod). Flask breaks; all three knocked into catalepsy.
- Awakening: laboratory gone; dingy dome room; crack in glass; Chuck's cold body; gold "Superman duds" (metal harness, metal-cloth cape, doeskin sandals).
- Hitler mentioned; "panzers."

### Ch. II (Priestess Beth)
- Women of **Tucki Clan** — golden **Priestess Beth** (dust-gold hair, steel-blue eyes), warrior captain **Jain**, the **Mother Maatha**; obese breeders, worker castes.
- Chant of "Star-Spangled Banner" mangled ("Osé, can you see by the Daans' surly light").
- Male sacrificed (bedizened pet); Duane's gesture stops it.
- Fautnox = Fort Knox, Kentucky (footnote).
- The Mother calls them "Slumberers"; Duane = "Dwain."

### Ch. III (Attack)
- Daan = Venus; Daan invaders; "Jarg," "Taamuz," "Ibrim," "Tedhi."
- Methioprane requires swamp-musk, extinct.
- Records: "one evil Slumberer." Von Rath allies (Duane, Chuck, von Rath = "three brothers").
- Mount Rushmore-type "Place of the Gods" in 'Kota (Dakota).
- Wild Ones attack: men of Tizathy (America).
- Sleep length: from 1942 to year 3488 (1,546 years; "Thirty-Fifth Century").

### Ch. IV (Revelation)
- Wild Ones: hairy males; Jon leader; Beth wants to kill them; Duane's "Trojan horse"-style trick; Jon says "I am a Man!"
- Revelation read from holy records: Men once ruled, Women walled forts, war.
- Mount Rushmore = "Place of the Gods" (Jarg, Taamuz, Ibrim, Tedhi = George, Thomas, Teddy, Abraham).

### Ch. V (Captured)
- Beth chooses Steve as mate; "touching-of-mouths." Mother Mairlee of Lextun; Tensee Clans; Clina and Yana.
- Nearest Daan camp: Sinnaty (Cincinnati) — Reds (Cincinnati Reds; McKechnie); "Nedlunplaza" = Netherland Plaza.
- Party: Duane, Chuck, von Rath, Jain + 3 women, Beth.
- Glass bridge over Ohio; Daans (fish-like, webbed fingers); Daan captain; "Loovil" false origin story.

### Ch. VI (Rodrik of Mish-kin)
- Sinnaty (Cincinnati) ruins; Carew Tower; Nedlunplaza hotel; Daan elevator.
- Prisoners tower: Rodrik of Mish-kin (blond, Brotherhood spy), "ruler of prisoners."
- Jak of Norlinz (New Orleans).

### Ch. VII (Lady Loala)
- Steve beats Rodrik in "Marquis of Queensbury" fight; Rodrik yields, then kicks Steve; Steve's final punch KOs Rodrik. Steve becomes ruler; Jak lieutenant.
- Lady Loala: silver-haired Daan Overlord of Sinnaty; council members Malgro (hostile) and Okuno (sympathetic).
- Loala: "You shall move into my chambers!"

### Ch. VIII (Honor for Sale)
- Loala: Brotherhood; "Treatment"; she desires Steve as consort; demands he renounce race.

### Ch. IX (Rebel—and Die!)
- Steve goes on Brotherhood. Treatment cabinet (electric-chair-like); nerve image cylinder; destruction = instant death.
- Steve sent to Fautnox; Loala: "Slumberers" rumor.

### Ch. X (Brother Rodrik)
- Steve exposes Rodrik as spy; Rodrik taken prisoner.
- Tucki & Wild Ones & Clans mass at Fautnox (2,804 warriors). Attack on Louisville (Loovil); Daan ray weapons; Steve accepts Daan surrender; von Rath set Rodrik free.

### Ch. XI ("A Daniel Come to Judgment")
- Von Rath betrays Steve; Steve intends to confront him personally.
- Steve pursues Rodrik toward Sinnaty; captured by Daan patrol; judgment by Overlord **Okuno** (Chief Executioner); Okuno swaps brain cylinders; Rodrik executed in place of Steve (Rodrik dies).

### Ch. XII (Alter Ego)
- Okuno = Wiam of Kleevlun, earthman disguised as Daan. Changelings network; "Have you kinsmen on distant Terra?" / "The brave never lack for brethren."
- Loovil retaken; garrison exiled to Daan planet. Beth, Mother Maatha, Shuk of Bruklin, Chuck exiled to Daan. Von Rath wounded, recorded as "Ay-rik."
- Steve disguised as Captain Huumo (silver hair, webbed fingers).

### Ch. XIII (Spaceflight)
- Ship **Oalumuo**; Loala also aboard; Thaamo (young space-officer).
- Ten-day trip; observatory deck; atomic motors.

### Ch. XIV (Between Two Camps)
- Planet Daan; Supreme Council (three Masters); palace; Loala as Overlord; slave camp in equatorial swamps; "klaar" (swamp-musk).

### Ch. XV (Swamp Gold)
- Slave camp; Chief Warden Grudo; lieutenant Amarro (sympathetic); earthmen including Beth, Mother Maatha, Chuck, Jon, Lina (Tensee captain). Von Rath (amnesia, in hospitalization).
- Steve tells prisoners; they call him "Betrayer." Amarro stops riot.
- Chuck: swamp-musk = methioprane base ("klaar... Venusian for nuisance weed").

### Ch. XVI (A Friend in Need)
- Plan: prison barracks as laboratory; distillation unit requisitioned. Von Rath unmasks Steve. Grudo and Loala capture him; Loala: "Have you kinsmen..."? (no—Amarro asks).
- Amarro's password: "have you kinsmen on distant Terra?" / "The brave never lack for brethren, O Dwain!"

### Ch. XVII (Fortress in the Fen)
- Steve escapes to Amarro's island refuge (underground; laboratory and ultra-wave communicator). Okuno's uprising on Earth ordered.
- Steve lured out by Loala using Beth's voice; struck unconscious.

### Ch. XVIII (The Offer of Loala)
- Steve held in palace tower; before Masters; boast about "Slumberers"; Loala offers mental operation to erase Steve's Earth brain and give Daan brain.

### Ch. XIX (End of the Trail)
- Steve bargains: amnesty for rebels. Loala agrees; Masters' decree audioed. Von Rath attacks Steve with ray; Loala hit by ray (intended for Steve).

### Ch. XX ("And Thus Be It Ever...")
- Steve kills von Rath (strangles). Loala mortally wounded; Steve puts her in methioprane sleep. Chuck: barracks workers seized the Armada (methioprane in air outlets); fleet captured.
- Treaty: Earth independent; Daan armada split; slaves freed; Duane's charter; Beth; Mother Maatha; "Star-Spangled Banner" verses; "Thy hoam, O Thou Brave!"; final line: "For a woman always has the last word. So, too, it was in the old days...."
